examples.ko: 여행 가이드가 유명한 맛집을 소개해 줬어요.
examples.en: The tour guide recommended a famous restaurant to us.
I toured Gyeongbokgung, following the guide.
The guide was very kind, so it was nice.
I would like to book a guide who speaks English.

examples.ko: 가이드가 길을 알려 줘서 길을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: The guide showed us the way, so we did not get lost.

examples.ko: 다음 주에 가이드 없이 혼자 제주도를 여행해요.
examples.en: Next week I will travel around Jeju alone without a guide.

explain: 여행을 안내하는 사람을 '가이드'라고 하고, '투어 가이드'라고도 해요. 책은 '가이드북', 지켜야 할 기준은 '가이드라인'이라서 비슷하게 들려도 쓰임이 달라요. 박물관에서 설명해 주는 사람은 '도슨트'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The tour guide explained in Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가이드'와 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 분명하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'guide', a bit more explicit.

phrases.en: We followed the guide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여행에서 안내하는 사람 뒤를 따를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for following the person leading a tour.

phrases.en: I read a guidebook before the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 안내하는 책을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a book, not a person.

explain_en: A person who leads tours is a 'guide', also 'tour guide' (투어 가이드). A book is a '가이드북' and a set of standards is a '가이드라인', so they sound alike but are used differently. Someone who explains exhibits in a museum is often called a '도슨트'.

en: to go on a tour; to see the sights

examples.en: I go sightseeing in Seoul with a friend on the weekend.
I went sightseeing on Jeju Island with my family.
There are many people sightseeing around here.
I want to go sightseeing around the city for a day.
You need a map to go sightseeing on foot.

examples.ko: 관광하러 온 외국인이 사진을 찍고 있어요.
examples.en: A foreigner who came sightseeing is taking photos.

explain: '관광하다'는 앞에 장소가 와서 '서울을 관광하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '구경하다'나 '여행하다'를 더 많이 말해요. 같은 한자어로 '관광지', '관광객', '관광버스'가 있어요.

phrases.en: I look around Seoul with a friend on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '관광하다'보다 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more than 관광하다 in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: There are many tourists on this street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관광하러 온 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who comes to see the sights.

phrases.en: Jeju Island is a famous tourist spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관광하러 많이 가는 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a place that many people visit as sightseeing.

explain_en: '관광하다' takes a place before it, as in '서울을 관광하다'. In everyday talk people say '구경하다' or '여행하다' more often. The same root gives '관광지' (tourist spot), '관광객' (tourist) and '관광버스' (tour bus).

examples.en: A traffic police officer is directing cars at the intersection.
I asked a traffic police officer for directions.

examples.ko: 교통경찰은 신호등이 고장 나면 수신호로 차를 안내해요.
examples.en: When a traffic light is broken, traffic police direct cars with hand signals.
My childhood dream was to be a traffic police officer.
The car stopped when it saw the traffic officer's hand signal.

examples.ko: 눈이 오는 날에는 교통경찰도 바빠 보여요.
examples.en: On snowy days, even the traffic police look busy.

explain: 도로에서 차와 사람의 흐름을 안내하고 단속하는 경찰이에요. 일상에서 직접 부를 때는 그냥 '경찰관'이라고도 해요. 짝말로 '수신호', '교통정리'가 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I asked a police officer for directions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 직접 부르거나 말할 때 쓰는 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader everyday word for a police officer.

phrases.en: The drivers watched the traffic police's hand signals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 차를 안내하는 신호를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Hand signals used to direct cars.

phrases.en: It's raining, so the traffic police are directing traffic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가 막힐 때 길을 정리하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Directing cars when traffic is heavy.

explain_en: This is the police officer who guides and monitors the flow of cars and people on the road. When addressing one directly, you can also just say '경찰관'. Common companions are '수신호' (hand signals) and '교통정리' (traffic control).

examples.en: If you take the local bus, it is five minutes to the subway station.
The local bus in our neighborhood has a cheap fare.
I go to work by local bus every morning.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 마을버스가 오지 않아서 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: The local bus did not come on a rainy day, so I walked.
There is a local bus stop in front of my house.
I got off the local bus and transferred to the subway.

explain: 큰길을 오가는 '시내버스'보다 작고, 동네와 지하철역을 이어 줘요. 서울에서는 지하철이나 다른 버스와 환승이 되는 경우가 많아요. '타다', '내리다', '갈아타다'와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: The local shuttle bus stop is over there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마을버스를 타는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where you board the local shuttle bus.

phrases.en: I get off the subway and transfer to the local shuttle bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 교통수단에서 마을버스로 바꿔 탈 때 '으로 갈아타다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 으로 갈아타다 to say you transfer to the shuttle bus.

phrases.en: How much is the local shuttle bus fare?
phrases.nuance_ko: 버스 값을 물을 때 '요금'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 요금 when asking about the fare.

explain_en: It is smaller than a main-road city bus ('시내버스') and links neighborhoods with subway stations. In Seoul you can often transfer to the subway or other buses with it. It goes with '타다' (ride), '내리다' (get off) and '갈아타다' (transfer).

examples.en: The waiter brought us the menu.

examples.ko: 저는 웨이터에게 물을 더 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked the waiter for more water.

examples.ko: 그 식당의 웨이터는 주문을 아주 빨리 받아요.
examples.en: The waiter at that restaurant takes orders very quickly.
My older brother works as a waiter at a hotel every vacation.
The waiter is walking by busily carrying plates.

examples.ko: 영화에서 웨이터 역할을 한 배우가 유명해졌어요.
examples.en: The actor who played a waiter in the movie became famous.

explain: 한국 식당에서는 직원을 부를 때 '웨이터' 대신 '저기요'나 '사장님', '이모'라고 불러요. 웨이터는 주로 호텔이나 큰 레스토랑의 직원을 말해요. 여자 직원은 '웨이트리스'라고도 하지만 요즘은 '직원'이라고 많이 해요.

phrases.en: I worked as a waiter during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업으로 일한다고 말할 때 '-로 일하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -로 일하다 to say what job someone does.

phrases.en: The hotel waiter brought the food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웨이터는 호텔 같은 곳에서 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: 웨이터 fits well in places like hotels.

phrases.en: The restaurant staff member was very kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웨이터 대신 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more than 웨이터 in everyday talk.

explain_en: In Korean restaurants you call staff with 저기요, 사장님, or 이모 rather than 웨이터. The word is used mostly for staff at hotels or larger restaurants. A woman can be called 웨이트리스, but 직원 is used more now.

en: to synthesize; to sum up; to combine into a whole

examples.en: I decided after putting together everyone's opinions.

examples.ko: 두 기사를 종합하면 사고 원인이 분명해요.
examples.en: Taking the two articles together, the cause of the accident is clear.

examples.ko: 조사 결과를 종합해 보니 만족도가 높았어요.
examples.en: When I summed up the survey results, satisfaction was high.
The ability to synthesize information is really important.

examples.ko: 오늘 회의 내용은 제가 종합해 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll sum up today's meeting for you.
When I combined my friends' stories, I found the answer.

explain: '모으다'는 물건에도 쓰지만 '종합하다'는 의견, 정보, 결과를 하나로 묶어 결론을 낼 때 써요. 반대로 나누어 살피는 것은 '분석하다'예요. '종합 우승'처럼 명사 '종합'으로도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I looked at the test results as a whole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 내용을 한꺼번에 모아서 살펴볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking at several things combined.
phrases.en_equiv: to look at as a whole

phrases.en: Putting all the stories together, he is right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결론을 말하기 전에 쓰는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A linking phrase used before stating a conclusion.

phrases.en: Our class won the overall championship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 경기의 결과를 합쳐서 나온 우승이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A win based on the combined results of many events.

explain_en: '모으다' works for objects too, but '종합하다' is for bringing opinions, information or results together into one conclusion. Looking at the parts separately is '분석하다'. The noun '종합' also appears often, as in '종합 우승' (overall victory).

examples.en: I took my foreign friend to a Korean restaurant.
There are many good Korean restaurants in this neighborhood.
I had lunch at the Korean restaurant in front of my office.
This Korean restaurant's menu also has bibimbap.

examples.ko: 부모님과 함께 갈 조용한 한식당을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for a quiet Korean restaurant to go to with my parents.
I like Korean restaurants because they bring out many side dishes.

explain: 한국 음식을 파는 식당 전체를 두루 말해요. 해외에서 한국 음식점을 말할 때 특히 자주 쓰고, 코스로 나오는 '한정식집'과는 조금 달라요.

phrases.en: I had lunch at a Korean restaurant nearby.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한식당'보다 조금 편하게 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds a bit more casual than 한식당.

phrases.en: We decided to go to a Korean restaurant this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가는 곳을 말할 때 쓰는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase for saying where you go.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to a Korean restaurant

phrases.en: I ate bibimbap at a Korean restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식사 장소를 말할 때 '에서'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에서 to name where you ate.
phrases.en_equiv: to eat at a Korean restaurant

explain_en: It broadly means any restaurant serving Korean food, and it is handy when talking about Korean restaurants abroad. It is a bit different from a '한정식집', which serves full-course Korean meals.
